sam (sec-eng): FYI were getting SAML assertion decrypt failures upstream and SCIM provisioning for a set of tenants is failing with KMS AccessDenied. Not seeing the usual "key not found" pattern.

ira (infra): paste a log snippet? region?

sam (sec-eng): region eu-central-1 for affected tenants. From provisioner on host eu-central-1b: 

```
2026-09-09T02:11:03Z provisioner[pid=712]: ERROR role.apply tenant=helios user=marc err="KMS:Decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException principal=svc-provisioner@redwood iam-role=provisioner-service-role action=kms:Decrypt key=arn:aws:kms:eu-central-1:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01" corr=tx-aa77
2026-09-09T02:11:03Z provisioner[pid=712]: WARN queued retry deprov=id=2f4b backoff=5s
2026-09-09T02:11:05Z provisioner[pid=712]: INFO scim/patch -> 204
```

noah (sre): AccessDenied not key-missing. That smells like an IAM policy change. Any recent infra PRs touching IAM or tf? deploy-bot, any rollouts last night?

deploy-bot: Deployment: terraform/apply #tf-6689 merged by @ira (infra) at 2026-09-09T00:12:00Z. Changes: minor role cleanup for "provisioner-service-role" and removal of unused inline policies.

sam (sec-eng): hmm. I also checked CloudTrail and see a series of `kms:Decrypt` "AccessDenied" events around 02:11 that map to that principal. audit-bot, did we lose any KMS audit entries or see deny spikes?

audit-bot: KMS audit:deny spike detected 2026-09-09T02:10:50Z - 02:12:10Z, service=provisioner, count=48, reason=AccessDenied.

ira (infra): ok reopening the TF PR now. If the inline policy that allowed `kms:Decrypt` was removed, that explains it. Can someone run `aws iam get-role-policy --role-name provisioner-service-role` and paste effective policy?

noah (sre): running on bastion and grabbing the policy, pushing output to /tmp/prov-role-policy.json. Policy shows we only have `kms:GenerateDataKey` and not `kms:Decrypt` for that key arn. Looks like the cleanup removed `kms:Decrypt` scoped to the provisioning key.

sam (sec-eng): that explains why SCIM returns 204 (agent accepted POST) but role.apply (which needs to decrypt a token or verify signature) fails. We need a rollback ASAP.

ira (infra): initiating emergency revert: reapply previous role policy that included `kms:Decrypt` and push new TF apply with emergency tag. Oncall @ira-africa will watch.

deploy-bot: terraform/apply #tf-6689 reverted by @ira at 2026-09-09T02:25:10Z; plan applied.

noah (sre): restarted provisioner on the three impacted hosts to pick up creds; seeing KMS:Decrypt success lines at 02:26 and queued deprov processing. Queues draining.

sam (sec-eng): collecting evidence bundle for compliance: CloudTrail deny logs, provisioner logs, terraform diff, and the role policy before/after. Uploading to /shared/sec-incidents/1971239999/. Note: include correlation ids corr=tx-* and scrub user emails.

ira (infra): postmortem notes: root cause = overly aggressive IAM cleanup removed necessary kms:Decrypt permission from `provisioner-service-role`. Contributing factors: no automated IAM policy unit test for crypto-related service role, and rollout lacked a canary check that exercised `kms:Decrypt` against the production key.

sam (sec-eng): mitigations: 1) add terraform plan-time policy linter to detect removal of kms permissions for roles that have active service principals; 2) add a pre-apply canary step that runs `kms:Decrypt` using a service account in a staging-like environment for any changes removing kms actions; 3) alert on KMS AccessDenied spikes tied to provisioner; 4) add a low-risk fail-fast in provisioner so that if crypto ops return AccessDenied we surface a clearer operational error and block further deprovisions to avoid long retry queues.

noah (sre): also create an automated smoke test in the rollout pipeline that performs one role.apply flow against a canary tenant when IAM changes touch `provisioner-service-role` or related policies.

ira (infra): opened PRs: #tf-6690 (policy linter), #ops-337 (canary decrypt check). Assigning @ira to land linter, @noah for smoke test, @sam for compliance evidence and runbook update.

securitybot: Incident recorded INC-20260909-3001 severity=medium status=resolved

sam (sec-eng): thanks team. Follow-ups scheduled on the next infra-sre triage to ensure IAM test coverage before policy cleanups. If anything shows up, please reopen. :thumbsup:
